summary:
[  edit  ]
NOTE
OS:  This operator is only supported under the  Microsoft Windows  operating system.
Hardware:  This operator only works with  Nvidia GPUs .
NVIDIA Flow is a volumetric fluid based simulation of a burning gas system. The user controls the 3 main factors of temperature, fuel, and smoke to create fire and smoke simulations.
The Nvidia Flow  TOP  calculates the Flow simulation and renders it. It requires a  Nvidia Flow Emitter COMP  to emit gas into the Flow simulation.
See also  Nvidia Flow Emitter COMP ,  Nvidia Flow .
Read more here  Nvidia Flow Artist Tools

inputs.description: Background Image  - Texture the Flow simulation will be overlayed onto.
Depth Map  - A  Depth TOP  to obscure parts of the Flow Simulation.

parameters.label: Initialize
parameters.name: initialize
parameters.description: Initializes the simulation.

parameters.label: Start
parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Starts the simulation playback.

parameters.label: Play
parameters.name: play
parameters.description: The simulation only steps forward when Play = On, when off the simulation is paused.

parameters.label: Camera
parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: Specify the  Camera COMP  to view the simulation from. Note: Must be camera with Projection = Perspective.

parameters.label: Flow Emitters
parameters.name: emitters
parameters.description: Specify the  Nvidia Flow Emitter COMPs  to include in the simulation.

parameters.label: Sim Position
parameters.name: simposition
parameters.description: ⊞  - The position of the simulation volume's center, in the world. The simulation cannot extend outside of the volume.

parameters.label: Sim Size
parameters.name: simsize
parameters.description: ⊞  - The size of the simulation volume in the world. The simulation cannot extend outside of the volume. Also controls the size of simulation blocks, so the total number of blocks in the volume stays the same. Smaller size blocks will require more blocks for the same size simulation. This increases accuracy but makes the simulation more taxing on the  GPU  as there are more blocks to calculate.

parameters.label: Mem Usage
parameters.name: memusage
parameters.description: Controls relative memory usage, the fraction of the total simulation blocks that will be allocated. Most simulations will not fill the simulation volume uniformly, so only a small value is needed. High values will cause extremely high memory usage.

parameters.label: Show Blocks
parameters.name: showblocks
parameters.description: Displays the simulation blocks being used. Useful for debugging or optimizing your Flow simulation. Also shows the edges of the simulation volume.

parameters.label: Show Emit Bounds
parameters.name: showemitbounds
parameters.description: Displays the bounds of the emitters.

parameters.label: Show Shapes
parameters.name: showshapes
parameters.description: Displays the shapes of the emitters.

parameters.label: Speed
parameters.name: speed
parameters.description: Controls the update rate of the simulation.

parameters.label: Max Simulation Steps
parameters.name: maxsteps
parameters.description: Maximum number of simulation steps per update. A higher number of steps will increase quality for fast moving object at the cost of performance.

parameters.label: Render Mode
parameters.name: rendermode
parameters.description: Provides two debug render modes in addition to the default of Density. Debug Density gives a "rainbow" render, where density is mapped to a colour, and Dubug Velocity converts velocity xyz to an rgb colour.

parameters.label: Gravity
parameters.name: gravity
parameters.description: ⊞  - Gravity direction for use with Buoyancy parameter, where amount controls strength of buoyancy force.

parameters.label: Velocity Damping
parameters.name: veldamping
parameters.description: Higher values reduce velocity faster. Uses exponential decay curve.

parameters.label: Velocity Fade
parameters.name: velfade
parameters.description: Compared to damping, fade reduces low velocity values faster. Fade velocity rate is in units per second.

parameters.label: Vel MacCormack Blend
parameters.name: velmaccormackblend
parameters.description: Higher values make a sharper appearance, but with more artifacts.

parameters.label: Smoke Damping
parameters.name: smokedamping
parameters.description: Higher values reduce smoke faster. Uses exponential decay curve.

parameters.label: Smoke Fade
parameters.name: smokefade
parameters.description: Compared to damping, fade reduces low smoke values faster. Fade velocity rate is in units per second.

parameters.label: Smoke MacCormack Blend
parameters.name: smokemaccormackblend
parameters.description: Higher values make a sharper appearance, but with more artifacts.

parameters.label: Temp Damping
parameters.name: tempdamping
parameters.description: Higher values reduce temperature faster. Uses exponential decay curve.

parameters.label: Temp Fade
parameters.name: tempfade
parameters.description: Compared to damping, fade reduces low temperature values faster. Fade velocity rate is in units per second.

parameters.label: Fuel Damping
parameters.name: fueldamping
parameters.description: Higher values reduce fuel faster. Uses exponential decay curve.

parameters.label: Fuel Fade
parameters.name: fuelfade
parameters.description: Compared to damping, fade reduces low fuel values faster. Fade velocity rate is in units per second.

parameters.label: Vorticity Strength
parameters.name: vortstrength
parameters.description: Controls amount of rotation turbulence as a multiplier, a value of 0 will result in no vorticity. High values increase turbulent flow while low values increase laminar flow.

parameters.label: Vorticity from Velocity
parameters.name: vortfromvel
parameters.description: Amount of vorticity added from velocity.

parameters.label: Vorticity from Smoke
parameters.name: vortfromsmoke
parameters.description: Amount of vorticity added from smoke.

parameters.label: Vorticity from Temp
parameters.name: vortfromtemp
parameters.description: Amount of vorticity added from temperature.

parameters.label: Vorticity from Fuel
parameters.name: vortfromfuel
parameters.description: Amount of vorticity added from fuel.

parameters.label: Vorticity Constant
parameters.name: vortconstant
parameters.description: The baseline vorticity in the simulation.

parameters.label: Ignition Temp
parameters.name: ignitiontemp
parameters.description: Specify the minimum temperature required for combustion.

parameters.label: Burn per Temp
parameters.name: burnpertemp
parameters.description: Control how much fuel is burned for a given temperature level. Lower Burn per Temp may result in some fuel not burning completely at a certain temperature.

parameters.label: Smoke per Burn
parameters.name: smokeperburn
parameters.description: Controls amount of smoke generated for each unit of combustion (per burn).

parameters.label: Temp per Burn
parameters.name: tempperburn
parameters.description: Controls amount of temperature generated for each unit of combustion (per burn).

parameters.label: Fuel per Burn
parameters.name: fuelperburn
parameters.description: Controls amount of fuel used for each unit of combustion (per burn).

parameters.label: Buoyancy
parameters.name: buoyancy
parameters.description: Works in conjunction with the parameter Gravity above which sets a vector for use by Buoyancy. Higher values result in greater effect by the Gravity parameter.

parameters.label: Cooling Rate
parameters.name: coolingrate
parameters.description: The rate of cooling in the system, exponential.

parameters.label: Expansion
parameters.name: expansion
parameters.description: Controls the amount the system's gaseous volume expands.

parameters.label: Velocity Alloc Weight
parameters.name: velallocweight
parameters.description: If zero, block allocation and deallocation depend on an internal threshold and weighting of Velocity. If non-zero,  block allocation and deallocation will be affected by the value of Velocity Alloc Threshold.

parameters.label: Velocity Alloc Threshold
parameters.name: velallocthreshold
parameters.description: If Velocity Alloc Weight is non-zero, block allocation and deallocation is based on this value. In particular, if the velocity magnitude is below this threshold, the block will be deallocated, unless smoke and fuel thresholding (see below) are active.

parameters.label: Smoke Alloc Weight
parameters.name: smokeallocweight
parameters.description: If zero, block allocation and deallocation depend on an internal threshold and weighting of Smoke density. If non-zero, smoke density affects block allocation and deallocation based on the value of Smoke Alloc Threshold.

parameters.label: Smoke Alloc Threshold
parameters.name: smokeallocthreshold
parameters.description: If Smoke Alloc Weight is non-zero, block allocation and deallocation is based on this value. In particular, if the Smoke density is below this threshold, the block will be deallocated, unless velocity and fuel thresholding are active.

parameters.label: Fuel Alloc Weight
parameters.name: fuelallocweight
parameters.description: If zero, block allocation and deallocation depend on an internal threshold and weighting of fuel density. If non-zero, fuel density affects block allocation and deallocation based on the value of Fuel Alloc Threshold.

parameters.label: Fuel Alloc Threshold
parameters.name: fuelallocthreshold
parameters.description: If Fuel Alloc Weight is non-zero, block allocation and deallocation is based on this value. In particular, if the Smoke density is below this threshold, the block will be deallocated, unless velocity and smoke thresholding are active.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.name: enableshadow
parameters.description: Enables Volume shadow rendering for the simulation. Shadowing generates light intensity values that overwrite the "burn" channel of the grid. Values range from 0 to 1, where 0 is fully shadowed. Shadow visibilty can be controlled by enabling 'Override Emitter Intensity Mask' or by adjusting the 'Burn Intensity Mask', 'Burn Alpha Mask', and 'Burn Color Mask' in  Nvidia Flow Emitter COMP

parameters.label: Draw Debug
parameters.name: drawshadowdebug
parameters.description: Displays the volume shadow blocks being used. Useful for debugging or optimizing.

parameters.label: Override Emitter Intensity Mask
parameters.name: overrideemitter
parameters.description: Automatically adjusts the emitters' render material, so volume shadows are visible. Will override 'Burn Intensity Mask' and 'Intensity Bias' of emitters.

parameters.label: Light
parameters.name: light
parameters.description: The light source used to generate volume shadow. The light should be a shadow caster. Only the position and orientation of the light are used, color and intensity are ignored.

parameters.label: Shadow  Resolution
parameters.name: shadowresolution
parameters.description: The resolution of the shadow map volume texture. The texture is allocated as a cube, so there will be space for shadowresolution^3 blocks.

parameters.label: Min Memory Usage
parameters.name: shadowminusage
parameters.description: The initial fraction of volume shadow blocks to allocate memory for.

parameters.label: Max Memory Usage
parameters.name: shadowmaxusage
parameters.description: The maximum fraction of volume shadow blocks to allocate memory for.

parameters.label: Intensity Scale
parameters.name: shadowintensityscale
parameters.description: Scales how dark the shadow will be.

parameters.label: Min Intensity
parameters.name: shadowminintensity
parameters.description: A lower limit for shadow intensity.

parameters.label: Burn Blend Mask
parameters.name: shadowburnmask
parameters.description: Allows the burn value in the simulation to control the blend strength of the shadow. Postive values mean burn increases the blend strength, negative values mean burn decreases the blend strength

parameters.label: Smoke Blend Mask
parameters.name: shadowsmokemask
parameters.description: Allows the smoke value in the simulation to control the blend strength of the shadow. Postive values mean smoke increases the blend strength, negative values mean smoke decreases the blend strength

parameters.label: Temp Blend Mask
parameters.name: shadowtempmask
parameters.description: Allows the temperature value in the simulation to control the blend strength of the shadow. Postive values mean temp increases the blend strength, negative values mean temp decreases the blend strength

parameters.label: Fuel Blend Mask
parameters.name: shadowfuelmask
parameters.description: Allows the fuel value in the simulation to control the blend strength of the shadow. Postive values mean fuel increases the blend strength, negative values mean fuel decreases the blend strength

parameters.label: Blend Bias
parameters.name: shadowblendbias
parameters.description: An offset that increases or decreases the blend strength by a constant amount. Parts of the grid with a blend value over 1 will have shadows. Parts of the grid with blend value under 1 will not have shadows. Blend values between 0 and 1 scale the strength of shadow.

parameters.label: Output  Resolution
parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - quickly change the resolution of the  TOP 's data.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution

parameters.label: Eighth
parameters.name: eighth
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Quarter
parameters.name: quarter
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Half
parameters.name: half
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 2X
parameters.name: 2x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 4X
parameters.name: 4x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 8X
parameters.name: 8x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Grow or shrink the input resolution to fit this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit the input resolution to be not larger than this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Directly control the width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine how the  TOP  image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.name: best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail. When the input is 32-bit float format, only nearest filtering will be used (regardless of what is selected).

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the  GLSL TOP  when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected  TOP 's image.

parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the  TOP  will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to  Pixel Formats  for more information.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace. Note that this does  not  apply an sRGB curve to the pixel values, it only stores them using an sRGB curve. This means more data is used for the darker values and less for the brighter values. When the values are read downstream they will be converted back to linear. For more information refer to  sRGB .

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgb10a2fixed
parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue  Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono8fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono16fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono)
parameters.name: mono16float
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono)
parameters.name: mono32float
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.name: rg8fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.name: rg16fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RG)
parameters.name: rg16float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RG)
parameters.name: rg32float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (A)
parameters.name: a8fixed
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 8-bits per channel, 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (A)
parameters.name: a16fixed
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (A)
parameters.name: a16float
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (A)
parameters.name: a32float
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 32-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha8fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha16fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha16float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha32float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: Input 0: Background Image

parameters.label: aspectx

parameters.label: depth

parameters.label: gpu_memory_used

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.description: speed, many-core processor of the graphics card/chip that takes geometry, images and data from the CPU and creates images and processed data.

parameters.label: The width and height of an image in pixels. Most TOPs, like the  Movie File In TOP  can set the image resolution. See  Aspect Ratio  for the width/height ratio of an image, taking into account non
